newsitem.title: USA: Planned White House Mideast summit talks delayed.
newsitem.headline: Planned White House Mideast summit talks delayed.

text.p: Leaders of the United States, Israel, Jordan and the Palestinians delayed planned Middle East summit talks at the White House on Tuesday as deputies tried to resolve Israeli-Palestinian differences.

White House spokesman Mike McCurry said Secretary of State Warren Christopher was conducting a lower-level summit session at the State Department and added, "The recommendation is that they not wander over here until they do some more work."

President Bill Clinton had planned a late morning meeting with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and King Hussein of Jordan. But Clinton was "on standby and waiting to see what kind of progress they (lower-level officials) make," McCurry said.
But McCurry refused to rule out the possibility that the summit talks would continue beyond Wednesday, telling reporters, "I have no idea how long they will last."

Clinton, less than five weeks away from the Nov. 5 U.S. presidential election, was scheduled to go to New York State on Thursday to prepare for a campaign debate with Republican challenger Bob Dole on Sunday.
